title: Describe a photo slowly
description: Turning a photograph into words is a quiet writing exercise that sharpens your eye for detail.

body.heading: Look longer than feels natural
paragraphs: Choose any photo: one on your phone, one in a book, one on a wall. Look at it for a full minute before writing. Notice what you missed in the first glance: background objects, expressions, light, small signs of the moment before and after.
Then write a description for someone who will never see the image. Plain words are fine. The goal is attention, not poetry.

body.heading: Go layer by layer
paragraphs: Start with the obvious: who or what, where, when it might be. Then move to details: colours, textures, what is worn or weathered. Finish with the feeling of the scene and one thing you are unsure about.
This exercise pays rent everywhere: stories get richer, essays get clearer, and even messages to friends get more vivid. Ten slow minutes is plenty.

takeaway: One photo, one minute of looking, one honest paragraph of words.
